title: The farewell sermon, in full
hook: at Arafah: your blood and property are sacred, treat women well, all of you are from Adam, and Adam from dust

segments.voice: Yesterday, Najran's Christians prayed in the mosque: let them be. Your line was: guests in the mosque.

The plain of Arafah, outside Mecca, on the day of the pilgrimage. The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, is on what Muslims call the farewell pilgrimage. Jabir ibn Abdullah, in Sahih Muslim, tells how he rides into the valley and speaks to the people. His first words tie three sacred things together: your blood and your property are sacred to you, as sacred as this day of yours, in this month of yours, in this city of yours. Today: the farewell sermon.
screen: `THE PLAIN OF ARAFAH.` → `HE SPEAKS TO THE PEOPLE.` → `AS SACRED AS THIS DAY.`

segments.voice: The sermon isn't one document; its lines are spread across the hadith collections, each narrator keeping a part. Jabir's account keeps his words about women: be mindful of God in how you treat them, for you have taken them on a trust from God. The next day, the day of sacrifice at Mina, Bukhari reports him asking: what day is this? What month? What city? In Abu Bakrah's report, each time the crowd answers: Allah and His messenger know best. Then: your blood, your property and your honor are as sacred to one another as this day, in this month, in this city. A sacred day, month and city, laid over every person in front of him. In reports in Ahmad and al-Tirmidhi, which some readers gather into the sermon, he says people are all children of Adam, and Adam was made from dust. No Arab has any merit over a non-Arab, nor a non-Arab over an Arab, no light-skinned person over a dark-skinned one, nor the reverse, except by mindfulness of God. The Qur'an says something close in surah forty-nine: humankind was made into nations and tribes so that they might know one another, and the noblest in God's sight is the most mindful of Him. In Jabir's account, he asks what they will say of him; they answer that he has conveyed the message. He raises his finger to the sky, points it toward the people, and says: O Allah, bear witness. And in Bukhari he tells those present to pass it on to those who are absent. That instruction is part of why you're hearing it now.
screen: `AS SACRED AS THIS DAY.` · `A TRUST FROM GOD.` · `CHILDREN OF ADAM, ADAM FROM DUST.` · `PASS IT TO THOSE ABSENT.` · then, large: `ALL FROM ADAM.`

segments.voice: If you can, read a translation of the farewell sermon from a reliable source, slowly; if not, hold just three lines: your blood and property are sacred; treat women well, as a trust; all of you are from Adam, and Adam from dust. Let each one sit for a few breaths, and if you pray, you can ask Allah to help you live by it.
Arafah, the plain of his last pilgrimage, where he declared each life and property sacred, and all people from Adam, and Adam from dust. Today's word.
Your line: all from Adam. The only rank named is mindfulness of God. Day seven hundred ninety-five, done.

howItsDone: Muslims read the farewell sermon from the hadith collections, where its parts are spread across several narrations, and it is recited and taught at the time of the hajj and in Friday sermons.

chat.says: What did the Prophet say on his farewell pilgrimage about race and rank?
options: All are from Adam, and Adam from dust; no merit except by mindfulness.
That a person's rank comes from the tribe and family they're born into.
That the wealthy are nearer to God, since wealth is a sign of favor.
chat.meaning: In reports in Ahmad and al-Tirmidhi: no Arab over a non-Arab, no light-skinned over dark, nor the reverse, except by mindfulness of God.

Arafah.meaning: a plain outside Mecca, central to the pilgrimage

Mina.meaning: a valley near Mecca, where the sacrifice is made

Jabir ibn Abdullah.meaning: a companion who described the farewell pilgrimage

Abu Bakrah.meaning: a companion who reported the sermon at Mina

al-Tirmidhi.meaning: compiler of a major hadith collection

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 67; 1741 (Abu Bakrah's report of the sermon at Mina: what day is this; sacred as this day; let the present inform the absent)
Sahih Muslim 1218 (Jabir's account of the farewell pilgrimage: the sermon at Arafah, blood and property sacred, women a trust, O Allah bear witness)
Musnad Ahmad 23489; Jami' al-Tirmidhi 3270 (children of Adam, Adam from dust; no Arab over non-Arab)

notes: Audit (2026-10-01): Mina sermon was the day after Arafah (day of sacrifice), not 'a few days later'; fixed. The 'Allah and His messenger know best' answers are Abu Bakrah's report (Bukhari 67, 1741); in Ibn Abbas's report (1739) the people answer 'a sacred day', so the citation and myth now name Abu Bakrah.

Editor: the questions (what day, month, city?) and 'pass it on to the absent' come from the sermon at Mina in Bukhari, not Arafah; Arafah lines now credited to Jabir in Muslim (sacred blood and property, women, 'O Allah, bear witness'); the Adam-from-dust line framed as reports some readers gather into the sermon; fork no longer places the question at Arafah.
All hadith numbers given from memory; confirm, especially Ahmad 23489 and Tirmidhi 3270.
Qur'an 49:13 paraphrased; Pickthall not quoted because exact wording was not certain.
The 'no Arab over non-Arab' line is in Ahmad and is not in Bukhari or Muslim; confirm grading language.
Title says 'in full' but the script gathers selected lines and sends the listener to a full translation in the practice; confirm acceptable.
'Raises his finger' follows Jabir's report in Muslim (pointing to the sky and then to the people); confirm.
'Recited and taught at the time of the hajj and in Friday sermons' in howItsDone: confirm.
Job 2: 'today we'll gather a few of them' became 'here are a few' (mascot voice); the practice no longer refers to the bell's time.
